title: Polar Bear, Polar Bear, What Do You Hear?
author: Bill Martin Jr

hero.name: Polar Bear
hero.description: White polar bear — generic animal but must be clearly white/arctic, not a brown bear; standard Boardmaker polar bear should suffice
hero.source_note: Use Boardmaker polar bear symbol; verify it is clearly white to distinguish from brown bear

ambiguous.issue: Could map to ear anatomy image or the action of hearing
ambiguous.reason: Book is built around the repeating question 'What do you hear?' — the listening/hearing action is correct

ambiguous.issue: Could be shown as sound waves, open mouth, or lion specifically
ambiguous.reason: Multiple animals roar in this book; a generic roar/loud sound image is preferred over a lion-specific one

notes: This book uses the same animals as Brown Bear Brown Bear but adds audio/sound vocabulary. The repeating structure 'X, X, what do you hear? I hear Y roaring/trumpeting/whistling at me' makes HEAR and animal sound words (roar, trumpet, whistle, growl, snort) highly functional — several are already in aac_extras and can be pulled from there. ZOOKEEPER replaces TEACHER from the final page spread where children imitate animals for the zookeeper; existing activity_images already has TEACHER which could substitute if zookeeper is unavailable. All 10 animals (polar bear, flamingo, peacock, walrus, elephant, hippopotamus, boa constrictor, lion, zebra, plus the children/teacher scene) are already in activity_images — only zookeeper and hear/roar need checking. BOA CONSTRICTOR may be labelled as SNAKE in Boardmaker; verify the image is a large constricting snake not a small generic snake for age-appropriate accuracy.
